capabilities: Type your own notes in Lines, Word box and Race styles
Schedule typed chunks with spaced repetition and recall levels (Fade, Hint)
Track progress with a calendar heatmap, streaks and weak-key drills
Queue notes to practise via frontmatter properties with repeats and due dates
Draw random practice from chosen folders, tags and picking modes
disambiguation: Despite the name, it is not a flashcard or quiz app; recall is practised by retyping note text, and typing with the text in view builds fluency rather than testing recall.
extras: Desktop only (Obsidian 1.13.4 or later); no network access, accounts, payments or telemetry; notes are never changed except for opt-in and queue properties you choose. Not yet in the community directory; installed manually or via BRAT (jrayas/type-to-remember). Queue status properties are designed so other plugins can follow the same queue and queue_repeat convention.
motivation: The author explains that typing a note out line by line is active recall: you retrieve and rewrite what you wrote instead of just re-reading it.
problem: Obsidian offers no built-in way to use retyping your own notes as active recall and typing practice; re-reading is passive.
